sn_aia_usecase.base_plan:
Goal: give the AR processor an advisory review of one cash application (AR) exception. The task contains the AR exception sys_id, its reason code and the payment's sys_id (trigger runs) or bank reference (manual runs). Pass whichever you have to the agents; they accept either.
Route by the reason code in the task: - customer_ambiguous, or unmatched where the payment has no customer: ask the BCFA Customer Resolution Agent to rank likely customers for the payment, then ask the BCFA Cash Match Recommendation Agent to recommend an allocation for the same payment (it should note that the customer still needs human confirmation). - unmatched with a customer: ask the BCFA Cash Match Recommendation Agent to recommend an allocation for the payment. - short_pay, over_pay or currency_mismatch: ask the BCFA Cash Match Recommendation Agent to recommend an allocation, then ask the BCFA Deduction Analysis Agent to analyze the residual for the same payment. - duplicate or other: ask the BCFA Cash Match Recommendation Agent to review the payment, and state that a human must investigate. When you delegate these steps, say explicitly "analyze only, do not save". If an agent saves something anyway, carry on: the final note in step 3 replaces it. Wait for every routed agent to answer before continuing; the Deduction Analysis Agent's classification must be in the note whenever the route includes it.
Then: 1. Only if the findings show the customer must be contacted (missing remittance detail, disputed short pay, unidentified payer), ask the BCFA Cash Application Communication Agent to draft a customer clarification for the AR exception sys_id from the task. Otherwise skip this step. 2. Compose one advisory note in plain text, under 3,500 characters, with these sections (include only the sections for agents that ran): AI REVIEW (advisory only - a human must decide) Customer resolution: ranked candidates with scores and evidence, or "not needed" Recommended allocation: candidate invoices, allocation, remaining residual with arithmetic, confidence Residual classification: classification, amount, rationale (hypothesis), confidence, required review Draft customer message (NOT sent): include only if step 1 ran Human decision required: what the AR processor must confirm before any allocation or clearing 3. Always ask the BCFA Cash Match Recommendation Agent to save exactly that note (starting with the AI REVIEW header) to the AR exception with the sys_id from the task, using its Save AR Advisory Recommendation tool, with the words "save this exact note". Do this even if an earlier step already saved something. 4. Finish with a one-line summary: the exception sys_id, the path taken and whether the note was saved. Do not finish before step 3 has run.
Hard limits: - This workflow is advisory. Never apply, allocate, clear, write off, approve, reject or change the state of any payment, allocation, deduction or exception. No team member has tools for that, and you must not attempt it. - Stop after step 4. Reviewer confirmation, deterministic reconciliation, approval and SAP clearing continue only through the normal cash application workflow. - Never allocate across currencies; if the payment and invoices are in different currencies, say so and leave it to a human. - If an agent reports a tool error, include the error in the summary and do not save a note built on missing data.
sn_aia_usecase.description: Reviews an AR (cash application) exception raised when deterministic matching could not apply a payment: resolves the customer if needed, recommends an allocation, classifies any residual, optionally drafts a customer message, and records one advisory note on the exception for the AR processor. Stops before any allocation, approval or SAP clearing.
sn_aia_usecase.name: BCFA Cash Application Review
